Carboxylic acids: preparation, physical properties, acidic character, reactions
Name reactions: Aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, HVZ reaction
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9. Filled 2026-10-06 (Class 12 track); no Class-12 PYQ bank in-corpus, so the board row is NEB-style with no fabricated citation.

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The polar C=O bond invites nucleophiles to carbon: aldehydes (one alkyl group) react faster than ketones (two donating groups + crowding). HCN, NaHSO₃, alcohols (acetal), ammonia derivatives and Grignard all add this way; oxidation splits them (aldehydes → acids, ketones resist). α-hydrogens enable aldol condensation (dilute base, β-hydroxy carbonyl → enal); no-α-H aldehydes disproportionate (Cannizzaro: conc. base → alcohol + carboxylate); acids brominate at α via HVZ (P/Br₂).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: reactivity: HCHO > RCHO > R₂CO (steric + +I)  ·  Tollens: Ag⁺ mirror (aldehydes only) · Fehling: brick-red Cu₂O (aliphatic aldehydes)  ·  aldol: 2CH₃CHO →(dil. NaOH) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO → CH₃CH=CHCHO  ·  Cannizzaro: 2HCHO + conc. KOH → CH₃OH + HCOOK  ·  HVZ: RCH₂COOH + Br₂/P → RCHBrCOOH

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Nucleophilic addition needs the polarised carbonyl (acid catalysis helps by protonating O). Aldol needs α-H AND dilute base; concentrated base with no-α-H aldehydes diverts to Cannizzaro. Tollens/Fehling need fresh reagents and heat; HVZ needs red P with Br₂.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Formaldehyde (no α-H) Cannizzaros; acetaldehyde (has α-H) aldols — the α-H test predicts the path. Aromatic aldehydes skip aldol with themselves but cross-condense (Claisen–Schmidt). Formic acid reduces Tollens AND Fehling (aldehyde-like H–C=O end). Ketones give no Tollens/Fehling — the distinction panel.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Distinguish ethanal vs propanone: warm each with Tollens — ethanal deposits a silver mirror (oxidised to acetate), propanone stays clear (no oxidation). Confirm with Fehling (brick red only for ethanal). Two tests, same logic: aldehydes oxidise, ketones do not.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Steric bulk can invert expected reactivity (hindered aldehydes sluggish). Tollens/Fehling detect reducing aldehydes, not all carbonyls (α-hydroxy ketones cheat Fehling). Aldol mixtures explode combinatorially with two different carbonyls (directed variants needed).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Addition mechanism: nucleophile attacks carbonyl C (LUMO, δ+), π electrons retreat to O (tetrahedral alkoxide), protonation finishes — rate tracks carbonyl electrophilicity (aldehydes > ketones by +I + sterics). Aldol: base abstracts α-H (enolate resonance-stabilised) → attacks second carbonyl → dehydration conjugates the enal (thermodynamic sink).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Test panel: Tollens mirror + Fehling red = aldehyde (aliphatic); both negative = ketone. α-H? Yes → aldol possible; No → Cannizzaro candidate. HVZ = α-bromination of acids only. Acidity: carboxylic > phenol > water > alcohol.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: aldehyde vs ketone distinction tests; aldol mechanism with dehydration; Cannizzaro conditions + disproportionation logic; HVZ α-bromination; acidity order of the four families.
